desc: Ideate multiset-matching reduction, fixed/wildcard counts, lower bound on S, and O(uA*uB) candidate-sum approach.

Verify the reduction R=max(0,aF+bF-N) and M(S)=Σ min(cntA[x],cntB[S-x]) against a brute-force enumerator for tiny N, including duplicates and x=S/2, and finalize a memory-bounded candidate-sum strategy.
Implement stdin parsing and split fixed values/wildcards; build frequency maps, max_fixed lower bound, and R with immediate edge-case handling.
Implement memory-bounded accumulation of M(s) over unique fixed A/B pair sums s>=max_fixed via packed-integer sort and linear aggregation, with early Yes when M(s)>=R.
Replace per-sum dict with packed (sum<<shift)|weight sorting strategy to bound memory over up to 4e6 candidate pairs.

Validate the current solution on the three provided samples and stress-test it against a brute-force enumerator over random small cases (including duplicates, all -1, one side all wildcard, no wildcards, N=2, wildcard imbalance, and x=S/2 self-matching); fix any discrepancies found.

Benchmark worst-case N=2000 with all-distinct fixed values (4e6 candidate pairs) for time and memory; optimize (early exit for need<=1, O(uA) probe, NumPy vectorized path with pure-Python fallback) to fit within limits.
